implementation_notes: `data class` generates the carrier's `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`copy`/`componentN`, and Kotlin's named arguments already let call sites label each value, so the combination replaces the hand-written parameter class completely; default values in the primary constructor replace overloads and `copy(...)` produces variations. Keep a plain class when you need custom equality, a private constructor with validation, or when a framework (JPA/Hibernate) requires a no-argument constructor and mutable state.
pitfalls: `var` components make equals/hashCode unstable: mutate a data class used as a map key and the entry becomes unreachable.
Destructuring (`val (x, y) = p`) is positional, so inserting a component silently rebinds callers - use property access unless the order is the canonical one.
JPA/Hibernate need a no-arg constructor; use the no-arg plugin or a plain class for entities instead of a data class.
